deployment_assumptions: Devices are considered difficult to update once deployed. Post-deployment access is assumed to be restricted, with a focus on design-time robustness and manufacturing controls. Devices operate in environments where stress and radiation may vary, impacting lattice stability.
open_questions: What specific environmental conditions (e.g., radiation levels, temperature variance) are expected in each deployment scenario?
Are there existing process controls or raw material specifications in place?
prioritization_summary: This assessment prioritizes threats based on their impact on electrical integrity, susceptibility to physical and environmental interference, and difficulty of remediation after deployment. Lattice defects and variations pose critical limitations on device performance and cannot easily be rectified in the field.

prioritized_actions.next_step: Initiate raw material sourcing and process control audit.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Fundamental to preventing critical lattice defects during manufacturing with irreversible consequences post-deployment.
prioritized_actions.title: Material Quality Assurance

prioritized_actions.next_step: Conduct feasibility study for radiation-hardened material selection.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Essential to preemptively counter radiation threats at the design level.
prioritized_actions.title: Radiation Hardening Design

prioritized_actions.next_step: Establish variability control metrics in the manufacturing process.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Address in conjunction with material controls to ensure lattice integrity from manufacturing onwards.
prioritized_actions.title: Lattice Defects Impacting Integrity

security_requirements.description: Ensure material purity and process control to minimize lattice defects.
security_requirements.design_robustness: End-to-end supply chain control to prevent introduction of material defects.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: Essential to prevent unrecoverable lattice defects and maintain device integrity.
security_requirements.requirement: Shall implement rigorous material inspection and control processes to ensure the purity and consistency of raw materials used in doping and junction formation.
security_requirements.title: Material Quality Assurance
security_requirements.verification_method: Regular audits and quality checks during production.

security_requirements.description: Incorporate design features to mitigate radiation effects on the lattice.
security_requirements.design_robustness: Intrinsic design robustness cannot be altered through external measures post-deployment.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: Design-level prevention is necessary for operation in high-radiation environments without external dependencies.
security_requirements.requirement: Should design lattice structures with materials and configurations resistant to radiation-induced degradation.
security_requirements.title: Radiation Hardening Design
security_requirements.verification_method: Radiation exposure testing under varied conditions.

security_requirements.description: Develop designs that manage temperature variations to maintain lattice integrity.
security_requirements.design_robustness: Thermal design must ensure device performance across all operational environments.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: Important for environments with variable temperatures to ensure device stability.
security_requirements.requirement: Shall include temperature regulation solutions to ensure stable operating conditions for lattice integrity.
security_requirements.title: Thermal Management Strategies

summary: This assessment focuses on the crystal lattice's role in ensuring stable electrical properties and controlled charge transport crucial for semiconductor function. Threats include lattice defects, radiation susceptibility, and environmental interference.

threats.attack_surface: Manufacturing process control and material quality.
threats.deployment_consequence: Defects embedded from the start cannot be corrected post-deployment.
threats.description: Defects in the crystal lattice can compromise the device's electrical properties, affecting performance and reliability.
threats.potential_impact: Unpredictable device behavior and reduced lifespan.
threats.priority_rationale: Given the impact on device reliability and the difficulty of correction post-manufacturing, this threat is a top priority.
threats.scenario: Process variations lead to lattice inconsistencies affecting semiconductor performance.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Introduced or exacerbated during manufacturing, impacting device uniformity and reliability.
threats.title: Lattice Defects Impacting Integrity

threats.deployment_consequence: Shielding is not feasible post-deployment; design-based solutions are needed.
threats.description: Radiation can alter the lattice structure, affecting charge carrier paths and device functionality.
threats.priority_rationale: High potential impact on deployed devices in radiation-rich environments.
threats.scenario: Deployed device exposed to cosmic rays or industrial radiation sources.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Environmental conditions at the deployment site expose the device to potential radiation.
threats.title: Susceptibility to Radiation

threats.deployment_consequence: Thermal issues cannot be easily remedied without redesign.
threats.description: Environmental stressors such as temperature can affect lattice uniformity, impacting charge carrier mobility.
threats.potential_impact: Decreased performance and increased failure rate.
threats.priority_rationale: Environmental robustness is crucial for reliable long-term performance.
threats.scenario: Operation in extreme temperature conditions causes lattice deformation.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Operational environments vary, affecting lattice stability.
threats.title: Charge Carrier Mobility Disruption
